newsitem.title: USA: Circuit City to open 60-65 superstores in year.
newsitem.headline: Circuit City to open 60-65 superstores in year.

text.p: Circuit City Stores Inc., announcing a drop in a key measure of December sales, said Tuesday it plans to open 60 to 65 superstores and replace 10 to 15 existing stores in the fiscal year beginning March 1.
The nation's largest retailer of brand-name consumer electronics and major appliances said it will open the stores in New York, Indianpolis and Dayton, Ohio, as well as in smaller markets.
Most of the stores will average about 34,000 square feet, the company said.
The Richmond, Va.-based company, also a leading retailer of personal computers and music software, said Monday it will open 40 stores by the end of 1999 in New York City, including 15 in 1997.

Circuit City said its December sales rose 4 percent to $1.17 billion from $1.13 billion in December 1995. However, its comparable store sales -- at stores that were open a year ago -- fell 13 percent.

"During December, industry weakness in consumer electronics and personal computer sales again produced an intense promotional climate and lower average retail prices," said Richard L. Sharp, Circuit City's chairman and chief executive officer.
"For Circuit City, comparable store sales growth in major appliances, digital satellite systems and big-screen televisions continued to partly offset the overall weakness."
Circuit City's stock gained 50 cents to $30 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
